title: Choose the dashboard's structure
question: The visual world stays (near-black, Instrument Serif display, Geist body, dusk palette for data). Pick how the five pages are organised and where the signature move lives.

options.label: Departure board
options.thesis: Every ranking is a departure board: rows of airlines, airports and routes in fixed tabular columns, with the delay rate as the lit column.
options.viewport: Top bar with the five pages as tabs and a live data strip (5,819,079 flights · stats built date); Overview opens on four KPI figures, then the 12 months as board rows each with its delay-rate bar.
options.risk: Charts (stacked causes, cascade line) must sit beside the boards as equals, or the page reads as a table app.

raised.raise: A re-sorted ranking moves rows in place and keeps the changed row lit, instead of redrawing the list.

options.label: Scope workbench
options.thesis: A persistent left column picks the airline and airport in scope; the canvas re-reads trend and raw flights for that scope.
options.viewport: Left rail with page links and the scope pickers (airline, origin); canvas with KPI row, monthly trend for the scope, and the index-backed flights table below.
options.risk: Only trend and /flights accept a scope; causes and rankings are network-wide, so the scope must say plainly what it does not filter.

options.label: Findings chapters
options.thesis: Each page opens with one finding as a serif sentence computed from the data, then the chart that proves it: a viva told in order.
options.viewport: Sticky chapter index on the left (01 Overview … 05 Model); the first viewport states '18.6% of 5.7M completed flights arrived 15+ minutes late' in large serif, with the monthly trend beneath.
options.risk: Finding sentences must be generated strictly from API values, never hand-written claims.
